gateway.compression: gzip -6 -n; each binary compressed separately, no archive overhead

before.algorithm: SHA256 of JSON sorted {path,sha256} file manifest; tracked and unignored new files

after.algorithm: SHA256 of JSON sorted {path,sha256} file manifest; tracked and unignored new files

uat.algorithm: SHA256 of JSON sorted {path,sha256} file manifest; tracked and unignored new files

scope: Same compiled engine for legacy serve and Go. Token auth over HTTP loopback, format-2 local filesystem, schedules/dashboard disabled, detached runs enabled. Sequential CLI data query and single-step command/shell echo hello workflow include CLI startup and wait for terminal success. Each workflow mode uses a fresh fixture, two warmup runs, then measured runs with equivalent growing history. The benign extension is loaded but not invoked. Module/filesystem caches warmed; no disk-cache flush. RSS/PSS include server/gateway and descendants discoverable at each sampling instant, excluding observer and transient CLI client. Read/idle measurements precede workflow writes. Source hashes identify the implementation snapshot, including uncommitted files; binary SHA256 identifies the exact artifacts measured.
limitations: Small fixtures and a trivial finite workflow only; shared host load uncontrolled; fixed mode order; Linux only. Memory sampling runs concurrently with workflow requests, scans /proc, and adds observer load. Observed peaks are lower bounds, may miss short-lived children, and are not atomic snapshots. No throughput, streaming/slow-client, cold OS/module-cache, representative vault/report corpus, or production workload claims. Five workflow samples make nearest-rank p95 equal the maximum. CPU is Linux accounting ticks over five-second observations, not normalized percentages. Compressed sizes are independent gzip6 files, not signed release archives. Builds are development artifacts, not release-promoted binaries.
